hn-50572503.t: Frostbite: A new CPU architecture discovered, designed and verified by AI
hn-50572503.s: Frostbite is a general-purpose CPU built around interaction nets, discovered, designed, and verified end-to-end by our AI systems, reaching 4.59x the performance-per-watt of a modern superscalar…
ex: In our previous post, Redwood, we showed that given an architecture, our AI systems could implement, verify, and deploy an inference accelerator in record time. However, similar to other scientific domains, we believe that AI systems, given the correct freedom and guardrails, can co-design software and hardware together, making optimizations across the stack and opening a design space so large it was previously inaccessible. We set out to answer the question: “Could our AI systems & tools lead to a novel hardware discovery that radically outperforms human-made designs?” Today, we're introducing Frostbite, a general-purpose CPU with a new instruction set built from the ground up. Frostbite exploits the properties of interaction nets, namely that every step is local, every dependency is explicit, and every value has exactly one owner, to reach a step-function gain in CPU performance that has long stagnated.

hn-50572348.t: Restricting AI agents in mobile operating systems platforms from capturing data
hn-50572348.s: Privacy is our mission; it’s why we exist, and we do everything we can to protect it. This means that we are restricting the latest AI agents built into mobile operating systems from potentially…
ex: Privacy is our mission; it’s why we exist, and we do everything we can to protect it. This means that we are restricting the latest AI agents built into mobile operating systems from potentially capturing and storing your Signal data. We’ve already had to do this once with Windows. Last year, we used screenshot blocking to prevent Microsoft’s Recall AI from taking and storing screenshots of your Signal messages on Windows 11 operating systems by default.1 We will now be taking similar measures to restrict agentic systems built into iOS 27 and on Android versions where we can detect an AI assistant attempting to read your Signal screen.2 The problem is similar to Microsoft Recall on Windows: Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems. This is a significant move.

hn-50581260.s: Inkling 2 Mini is an open-weights model small enough to run on your laptop. It loops its middle layers to reason more per token and reach answers in fewer tokens.
ex: Today we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, powerful model that’s small enough to run on your laptop. Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. Inkling 2 Mini leads every open-weights model with less than 100B total parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%). It runs faster than similarly performing models as well. Inkling 2 Mini is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 26.4B total parameters, 3.4B active, and 5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping. Looping allows the model to reason longer without writing its reasoning down, which matters for monitoring: our ability to oversee and understand what the model does by reading its chain of thought (CoT).

hn-50578794.t: Anthropic shares tank after IPO as the Nasdaq erases 2026 gains
hn-50578794.s: Anthropic’s record-setting IPO Thursday failed to restore investor confidence in the AI market.
ex: The surging stock market of 2026 capsized Friday, wiping out gains for the year in the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite while the broad S&P 500 and the Dow entered correction territory, meaning they have declined 10% from recent peaks. The dramatic sell-off is raising fresh fears about the viability of the AI investment wave that had powered stocks and economic growth for the first half of the year. Friday’s declines were led by Anthropic, whose blockbuster IPO just 24 hours earlier now feels like a blip after the stock lost 9%, wiping out hundreds of billions in paper wealth and putting shares just a few dollars above the IPO price. Nvidia also dragged markets lower, tumbling about 14% following a Reuters report that regulators are looking into accounting irregularities at the chip giant. With Friday’s losses of 3.7%, the S&P 500’s seven-day losing streak is its worst since the Covid pandemic; the index is now up less than 1% on the year.

hn-50574383.t: Global stock markets slump as Anthropic's record IPO fails to stem AI sell-off
hn-50574383.s: The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout
ex: The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory. Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal. Shares in the frontier AI company behind the Claude chatbot, which floated in the US on Thursday, fell by 9% on Friday, ceding most of the gains from the biggest initial public offering in history. They dropped to $88.30, towards the $83 level at which Anthropic priced its stock market debut. Anthropic’s first two days as a listed company have been volatile.

hn-50579331.t: We promoted developers into architects without informing them
hn-50579331.s: If you hate vibe coding, it’s because you’re still trying to do the old job. AI does what you ask and won’t push back on requirements that slows your app or delete tables you created for testing.
ex: Yesterday, I was debugging a performance problem with our Google Forms addon. It turned out my colleague had vibe coded the logging part, so that he could monitor the new installs every week. Monitoring new customers is the most important part of running a business, so he is absolutely right in doing that. Except, he was logging the user’s email and Google has severely restricted how much detail you can get about the user since last December. So, AI had written a series of try/catch statements: In our case, the right fix is simple. Log the timestamp, show the welcome screen first and tell marketing what they can’t get on install. But AI will never make that call for you, because it doesn’t know your users and it won’t push back on your requirements. That is the architect’s job. If you are a developer, the coding job is going away. But it doesn’t mean your job is going away.

hn-50575644.t: Why there are still no non-WebKit browsers on iOS
hn-50575644.s: Firefox on iPhone is growing fast across the world. This is especially true in the EU since 2024, when the EU Digital Markets Act (DMA) started requiring A
ex: Firefox on iPhone is growing fast across the world. This is especially true in the EU since 2024, when the EU Digital Markets Act (DMA) started requiring Apple to let people choose their default browser; millions have picked Firefox, and daily use on iOS has doubled. People want to choose the browser on their phone. But there remains an important limitation to what is available on iPhones: Apple forces all browsers on iOS to be built on Apple’s own browser engine. This has meant that companies like Mozilla cannot easily bring the full range of Firefox features and functionality to iPhone users because many of these are built within our browser engine, Gecko. iPhones and iPads are unique in having this restriction. On all other major operating systems, including Apple’s macOS, people can access the Gecko-powered version of Firefox. As a result of the DMA, Apple began allowing alternative browser engines on iOS in the EU.

hn-50581438.t: US SEC's Nvidia probe is examining potential accounting issues – sources
hn-50581438.s: Published on 11/20/2026 at 02:10 pm EST - Modified on 11/20/2026 at 02:17 pm EST
ex: Published on 11/20/2026 at 02:10 pm EST - Modified on 11/20/2026 at 02:17 pm EST NEW YORK/WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The US Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's accounting practices, said two people briefed on the matter, adding to the legal woes facing the scandal-hit chip giant. The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday reported that the SEC was probing Nvidia but said it could not ascertain the focus of the investigation. The people, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential issues, said SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing potential accounting issues at the company. A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment. Spokespeople for Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not immediately determine when the SEC opened its inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog is examining. Investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without resulting in enforcement action.

hn-50579297.s: how coding agents wrote 3M lines of code to implement and optimize LLM inference on an FPGA
ex: Or rather, I vibe-coded an FPGA into running an LLM. And it… just worked. One of the more entertaining things about programming recently is that coding agents let me work in entirely new domains by giving me access to new programming languages and paradigms. Lately, that has meant hacking on hardware, now that writing low-level software is much easier. So, in this blog post, I’m going to try to recount the experience of vibe coding an FPGA, going through a series of “oh shit” moments several times, and giving myself a new appreciation for what’s possible if you have a large token budget (thanks YC) and interesting problems to point the models at. I overheard some founders recently talk about how FPGAs work. I’ll admit I was relatively naive about them. I’d never really experimented with them in my startup or in college, so I knew little about them before. The basic idea I was familiar with: you can program a circuit into a reprogrammable chip.

hn-50576232.t: Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations
hn-50576232.s: This repository holds the paper Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations by L. Alpöge and T. Buckmaster and the Lean 4 formalization that accompanies it.
ex: This repository holds the paper Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations by L. Alpöge and T. Buckmaster and the Lean 4 formalization that accompanies it. - paper/finite-time-blow-up-navier-stokes.pdf: the paper (79 pages, version of 20 November 2026). - lean/: the Lean package (Lean v4.33.1 with Mathlib, at the revision pinned in lean/lakefile.toml). - lean/README.md explains how the formal statements relate to Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1, Corollary 7.2 and Appendix B of the paper, and where the formal proofs differ from the proofs of the paper. - lean/NOTICE says in words what each statement file contains and what is proved. The statement files at the top of lean/ give the definitions and state the theorems with sorry in place of their proofs; Solution.lean proves them from the library lean/Breakdown/.

hn-50569226.s: General purpose TLS and crypto library
ex: OpenSSL is a robust, commercial-grade, full-featured Open Source Toolkit for the Transport Layer Security (TLS, formerly SSL), Datagram TLS (DTLS), and QUIC protocols. The protocol implementations are based on a full-strength general purpose cryptographic library, which can also be used stand-alone. Also included is a cryptographic module validated to conform with FIPS standards. OpenSSL is descended from the SSLeay library developed by Eric A. Young and Tim J. Hudson. The official Home Page of the OpenSSL Project is [www.openssl.org]. - Overview - Download - Build and Install - Documentation - License - Support - Contributing - Legalities - libssl an implementation of all TLS protocol versions up to TLSv1.3 ([RFC 8446]), DTLS protocol versions up to DTLSv1.3 ([RFC 9147]) and the QUIC version 1 protocol ([RFC 9000]). - libcrypto a full-strength general purpose cryptographic library. It constitutes the basis of the TLS implementation, but can also be used independently.

hn-50581403.t: OpenComputer – an open source alternative to Devin
ex: OpenComputer is the open source, self hostable alternative to Devin. Mention @Computer in a Slack thread with a task, it works on its own computer, you & your team can watch and steer it as it goes, and the result lands as a pull request. It is open source from the compute layer up, so you can run all of it in your own cloud account, or start on OpenComputer Cloud in two minutes. We built it to feel as fast as Claude Code on your laptop: in our benchmark it opens PRs 3.3x faster than Devin. OpenComputer is built to be simple to self-host without giving up scale or security. The whole stack runs on a single VM, which we recommend locking down to outbound-only network access. The VM runs the gateway, Calvin: a thin bridge that listens for Slack events and starts a session with Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode, depending on your configuration. Each session is isolated with rootless Podman. Its state is written first to the VM's local disk, then persisted to a git-backed store.

hn-50579568.s: I am at the American Mathematical Society Executive Committee and Board of Trustees meeting now, and about to chair an hours-long meeting, but this is urgent, so I will try to get this out quickly.
ex: I am at the American Mathematical Society Executive Committee and Board of Trustees meeting now, and about to chair an hours-long meeting, but this is urgent, so I will try to get this out quickly. Alessandro Maria Masullo has a proposed proof of GRH, and Brian Conrad has been looking closely at it for months and gave extensive feedback which is being incorporated, and it is so far looking good to him. It is all human, with no AI. The hope was to have Brian work with Alessandro for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people. Now it seems best to put out the current draft. I hope people quickly check it, formalize, fill any small gaps if they occur. I really hope it works. I have great faith in Brian’s judgement, and Brian has put a lot of thought into checking what Alessandro has done. There is a long story to tell, but right now I want to get the file out. Here it is.

gh-1464126198.s: FastUnlock : Windows Narrator LockScreen Bypass 0day Vulnerability
ex: The vulnerability exist in the way how narrator handles UI in a locked account context, succesful exploitation results in bypassing bitlocker and executing code in the context of the lockscreen account "WsiAccount" It took a total of 5 minutes from finding this to breaching a fully encrypted bitlocker machine with Windows 11 26H2 November Patch installed, an issue caused by total negligence from Microsoft's side... The vulnerability seems to be extremely consistent in every machine I tested it in, in other words, if you know how to control narrator in the background properly or just press the correct combination of buttons, you will get code execution in the target machine as well. Obviously this needs physical access and at least one account in the machine to be linked to an online account, this breaks the guarantee that a properly secured bitlocker machine cannot be accessed even if the attacker has physical access so hold tight any windows machines until Microsoft patches this.

gh-1465523535.s: Chat with private AI models locally, powered by Open Webui Private Ai Desk.
ex: Open Webui Private Ai Desk is a self-contained AI workspace built for teams and individuals who want the power of modern language models without sending their data beyond their own infrastructure. It brings chat, document interaction, and model management together in a single, refined interface that feels effortless from the first session. Every conversation stays private by design, running entirely on your own hardware and terms. The result is a dependable AI desk that blends serious capability with the polish of a product built to be used every day. - OS: Windows 10 / 11 - Shell: PowerShell 5.1+ or PowerShell 7+ - Network: internet access to download the script - Privileges: standard user - Private by design: Run your entire AI workspace locally, keeping conversations, documents, and model interactions on your own infrastructure — no third-party exposure.
